2026-10-08.meal: Fish finger pitta pockets with slaw
2026-10-08.note: Moved from Monday. Early, quick tea before Francis's parents' evening appointment at 7:05pm

ingredients: 1/4 white or red cabbage, finely shredded
Ketchup or tartare sauce, to serve
steps: Air fry the fish fingers at 180°C for 10 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and piping hot. (Or oven at 200°C / 180°C fan for 12–15 minutes.)
While they cook, mix the cabbage and carrot with the mayonnaise and lemon juice to make the slaw. Season.
Warm the pittas briefly and split them open.
Fill each pitta with lettuce, 3 fish fingers and a spoonful of slaw.
Serve with ketchup or tartare sauce on the side.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: fish fingers and pitta plain, slaw on the side so she can dip or avoid it. Cut her pitta into fingers.

2026-10-09.note: Mathilda's gymnastics 9:30am & swimming 1:30pm today, evening's free — steak night

ingredients: Potatoes, for wedges (we have plenty in)
steps: Cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with a little oil and seasoning, and air fry at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp. (Or oven at 200°C/180°C fan for 25-30 minutes.)
Season the steaks well. Get a griddle or frying pan very hot.
Fry the mushrooms cut-side down for 4-5 minutes with the butter and garlic, until tender.
Cook the steaks for 2-3 minutes each side for medium-rare (longer if you like it more done), then rest for 5 minutes.
Steam or boil the broccoli for 4-5 minutes until just tender.
Slice the steak for the kids and serve everyone with their mushroom, broccoli and wedges.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her steak into small, well-done pieces and keep her mushroom plain.

2026-10-10.meal: Air-fryer breaded fish fillets with mash, peas & sweetcorn
2026-10-10.note: Free evening after this morning's hockey session & home match — family favourite

ingredients: 4 servings mash (fresh potatoes, or microwave pouches for speed)
Butter & milk, for the mash (if making fresh)
steps: Air fry the fish fillets at 190°C for 12-14 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and piping hot.
If making fresh mash, boil chunked potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, then mash with butter and a splash of milk.
Cook the peas and sweetcorn in a pan of boiling water for 4-5 minutes, or microwave.
Drain and serve everything together.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her fillet into pieces and check it's not too hot. Microwave mash pouches work well if it's been a long day.

2026-10-11.meal: Sweet potato & spinach dhal with rice
2026-10-11.note: U12 Yorks Performance hockey training 12-2:30pm today, evening's free — good day to batch cook extra for Wednesday's Hockey Academy Night

steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, lentils and stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils and sweet potato are soft.
Stir in the coconut milk and spinach and cook for 3-4 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Take out Mathilda's portion and 4 portions to cool for Wednesday before seasoning the rest.
Cook the rice and serve with the dhal.
Cool the 4 extra portions within an hour, cover and keep in the fridge for Wednesday (no need to freeze).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers plain and mash the sweet potato a little finer.

2026-10-12.meal: Slow-cooker gammon with parsley sauce, mash & peas
2026-10-12.note: Free day, nothing else on — note this makes 2 meat nights this week alongside Friday's steak. Alex may still be away for work (PO Visit) — keep a portion aside for him to reheat.

ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (or 1 tbsp dried)
steps: Put the gammon, onion and bay leaves in the slow cooker and pour over the water or stock.
Cover and cook on low for 5-6 hours, until the gammon is tender and shreds easily.
Lift out the gammon, rest for 5 minutes, then slice or shred, discarding any string and excess fat.
For the sauce, melt the butter in a pan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer for 3-4 minutes until thickened, then stir in the parsley.
Boil and mash the potatoes. Cook the peas for 4-5 minutes.
Serve the gammon with mash, peas and parsley sauce.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: rinse her portion briefly if the gammon's salty, and go light on the sauce. Keep a portion aside for Alex if he's away.

2026-10-14.meal: Reheat: Sunday's sweet potato & spinach dhal with rice
2026-10-14.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15-7:45pm (The Lindum) — quick reheat gets tea done either side of the run

steps: Tip the dhal into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8-10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4-5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the rice while the dhal heats.
Serve straightaway.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot before serving.

2026-10-15.meal: Garlic butter baked haddock with crushed new potatoes & peas
2026-10-15.note: Normal evening, nothing on for tea

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the new potatoes for 15-18 minutes until tender.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and a squeeze of lemon. Put the haddock on a lined tray and brush over the butter.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Cook the peas for the last 4 minutes of the potatoes.
Drain and lightly crush the potatoes with a fork, stir through the parsley and a knob of butter.
Serve the fish with the crushed potatoes, peas and lemon wedges.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: leave the garlic butter off her portion and check carefully for bones.
